videos.description:
Are squirrel-proof bird feeders a myth? Mostly, yes! Squirrels are smart, acrobatic, and persistent, so most feeders labeled "squirrel-proof" don't hold up. In this episode of Feeder Myths, Busted, we cover why weight-activated feeders work best, why the Squirrel Buster line by Brome stands out as truly squirrel-proof, how to use baffles with other feeders, and how far squirrels can jump (8 to 10 feet sideways, about 5.5 feet up) so you can place your feeders right. 🐿️🐦

videos.title: Do birds need water in winter? Yes! It's a common myth that birds don't need water once it gets cold
videos.description:
Do birds need water in winter? Yes! It's a common myth that birds don't need water once it gets cold. Birds drink year-round and rely on water to preen and maintain their feathers, which provide insulation in freezing temperatures. Eating snow or ice uses up valuable energy. Learn simple ways to give backyard birds open water in winter: a heated bird bath, a bird bath heater, or breaking up ice daily. 🐦❄️💧

Episode 5 of Feeder Myths, Busted from For The Wild Birds.

videos.title: Should you feed migrating birds? Yes! Fall migration myth busted. 🐦
videos.description:
Should you feed migrating birds? Yes! Fall migration myth busted. 🐦

Warblers, orioles, and hummingbirds are migrating south right now. When they stop at your bird feeder, they're refueling energy lost on long-distance flights. Migration depletes fat reserves quickly, so backyard feeders and flowers can help birds reach their wintering grounds. Keep your feeders full during fall migration!

Episode 2 of our Feeder Myths, Busted series. Subscribe for more backyard bird feeding tips! 🍂

videos.title: Does feeding birds in the fall stop them from migrating? No! Bird migration is triggered by shorteni
videos.description:
Does feeding birds in the fall stop them from migrating? No! Bird migration is triggered by shortening daylight hours (photoperiod), not by food supply. Keeping your bird feeders full in fall helps migrating birds build fat reserves for their journey and lets resident birds like cardinals, chickadees, and nuthatches know there's a steady food source through fall and winter. 🍂🐦

Feeder Myths, Busted: Episode 1 of our fall bird feeding myth series from For The Wild Birds.

videos.title: Why did the birds disappear from your feeders? It's molting season! During late summer and early fal
videos.description:
Why did the birds disappear from your feeders? It's molting season! During late summer and early fall, backyard birds lose and regrow their feathers, making it harder to escape predators. They hide out, especially in yards with little cover, and rely on natural food sources like seeds, berries, and insects instead of bird feeders. The good news: birds return to feeders as temperatures drop and natural food freezes. Learn why feeder activity slows down and why this is the perfect time to clean your bird feeders before fresh food goes back out. 🐦🪶

videos.description:
When should you take down your hummingbird feeder? Not yet! Hummingbirds are still migrating through backyards in late September, stopping to fuel up before Ruby-throated Hummingbirds make a 500-mile nonstop flight across the Gulf. Keep your hummingbird feeders out until two weeks after the first freeze to give them the energy they need. 🐦⛽
